title: The scalar-unit reduction equation at a single affine zero divisor
statement: Use the actual supported coefficients, finite twists, quotient $\phi:A_{E,b+1}\to A_{E,a+1}$, and scalar-unit predicate [def-amb-proetale-supported-coefficient-reduction], and the zero Cartier divisor $s:S\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_S$ [def-pur-finite-affine-orientation-comparison]. For a Cartier family $c$, a prime $\ell$, finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $a\le b$, and $\ell$ invertible on $\mathbf A^1_S$, define the reduction equation at $s$ as follows: there exist semilinear supported-constant and degree-one-twist maps $\eta,\theta$, sending every supported constant generator $z$ to $\bar z$ and every integral-root tensor $z\otimes x$ to $\bar z\otimes x$; both satisfy the full derived scalar-unit universal property; and the typed supported Ext square commutes: in Lean/Yoneda composition order, $\eta\,\operatorname{Res}_{\phi}(c_a)=c_b\,\theta$. This is the single-zero-divisor specialization of the existing Cartier reduction equation. Family references and size conventions are those of [def-pur-finite-orientation-scalar-presentation].
